\begin{tablenotes} \footnotesize
\item \textit{Notes:} Controls are child sex, BMI-for-age z-score, stunting, caregiver education, age and sex, household size, wealth, housing-quality and consumer-durables indices, electricity, land ownership, and food-security categories. Each first stage uses the exact corresponding second-stage sample.
\item The excluded-instrument $F$ tests $E_{is}=0$ conditional on all controls (one numerator degree of freedom); its conventional standard error matches Panel B. Partial $R^2$ measures the additional variation in MTI intake explained by $E_{is}$. HC1 uses heteroskedasticity-robust first-stage variance with a degrees-of-freedom correction.
\item Anderson--Rubin tests $H_0:\beta_{MTI}=0$ using a conventional $F$ test of $E_{is}$ in the reduced form, retaining validity under weak identification under the iid normal model; the HC1 $p$-value uses an asymptotic $\chi^2_1$ reference allowing heteroskedasticity. These test the employment effect, not instrument strength. These diagnostics do not address dependence within the four regional policy clusters. There is one excluded instrument and one endogenous regressor, so an overidentification test is unavailable.
\item Conventional standard errors are in parentheses. *** Significant at 1\%, ** at 5\%, * at 10\%.
\end{tablenotes}
